nitya: Heads-up — found a couple broken anchors on Troubleshooting > Rate Limits and the CLI repro for 429s is outdated (uses legacy header `X-Old-Rate`), which makes the curl snippet fail. Opening a tiny PR to fix anchors and replace the snippet with a reproducible curl + minimal backoff examples. PR incoming (#3421).

olivia: thanks — which anchors? can you paste the exact link+anchor so we can confirm the redirect behavior?

nitya: the page is https://docs.redwood.ai/troubleshooting/rate-limits and the anchor `#repro-locally` 404s — our docs host redirects `/troubleshooting/...` -> `/guides/...` and strips anchors. also the curl example omitted `-D -` so users can't see `Retry-After`, and the example uses `X-Old-Rate` in headers.

conor: If anchors are getting stripped by the redirect we should fix routing, but a docs patch is faster. please include a short "how to repro safely" that captures response headers and suggests parsing `Retry-After`. Keep netem instructions as a link, not inline.

nitya: PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/3421 — changes: fix anchors, add curl snippet that captures headers, add tiny Node/Python backoff examples, and a link to the ops netem quick-start (internal). requesting review from @olivia and @sam.

sam: assigning self to review. quick asks — keep examples minimal (one-liner curl + 3-line python/node). avoid deep netem how-to; link out to ops note instead.

nitya: agreed. pared down netem to a single sentence and linked to internal note: https://go.redwood/ops/netem-quick. also added a concise repro command: 

```bash
# reproduce token-window 429 locally (simulate burst)
TOKEN=...; curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -X POST "https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate" -d '{"prompt":"x","max_tokens":10}' -D - --max-time 8
```

olivia: looks much better. tiny nit — use `api.redwood.com` (you already updated) and make sure the curl JSON uses double quotes (yep). Also can we add a short note to explain `-D -` so readers know it's capturing headers?

nitya: added a 1-line explanation about `-D -` and a small python backoff snippet.

sam: I reviewed, left one nit about Retry-After parsing wording. can you add pseudo-code for parsing the header and doing exponential backoff with jitter? keep it short.

nitya: added this python snippet (3 lines) in PR: 

```python
import time, random
def backoff(attempt, base=0.5, cap=10):
    sleep = min(cap, base * 2**attempt)
    jitter = random.uniform(0, sleep*0.1)
    time.sleep(sleep + jitter)
# if resp.status_code == 429 and 'Retry-After' in resp.headers: time.sleep(int(resp.headers['Retry-After']))
```

conor: small suggestion — add a :warning: note that backoff windows should respect route SLA and not block upstream timeouts. maybe one sentence. :+1: otherwise.

olivia: LGTM besides that. Sam, can you /approve so we can merge and push to staging?

sam: /approve — merging after CI.

nitya: thanks all — I'll merge once CI passes, then ping #release for a quick staging deploy. adding a follow-up to audit other troubleshooting pages for similar anchor rot: tracking issue #3422. :shipit:

docs-bot: label added: needs-staging-sync

nitya: merging now, will watch CI and notify when staging is up. thanks for the quick reviews!
